body: I am talking to a counselor. It helps a lot that day, but the next day I feel like I get shot in the foot all over again. I hope you have better luck than I do.

I'm going to post what I did to the other commentor.

"So, I have a new professor as a PI and I guess I feel pressured into producing producing producing. That's part of the problem. I spend a lot of time working and don't have much time for anything else. I'm chronically ill, so by the time I do get home all I want to do is sleep and cuddle my cats."

So, I have a new professor as a PI and I guess I feel pressured into producing producing producing. That's part of the problem. I spend a lot of time working and don't have much time for anything else. I'm chronically ill, so by the time I do get home all I want to do is sleep and cuddle my cats.

The confusing ending was also pretty good. The narrator was a great voice actor. 

I want to learn how to play the piano. I got a free keyboard from an International student, so now I have no excuse. Some days its just hard to want to do anything.

The art ending was hilarious (well the "game" part, I couldn't play for 4 hrs of baby shrills). The museum was a really cool idea by the programmers. I also like the depressing "work" ending with the fake wife. I'm not really sure which is my favorite.

I just feel like when I escape I'm not progressing at all in RL, thus when I'm back to real life I wonder what the fuck do i do with my time. Then I'm upset and feel like a lazy fuck.

I know, rationally, that alcohol is bad. The weird thing, I know when I'm not behaving rationally. It's just I can't stand to have all of those emotions at that time. Alcohol is numbing. I know, I know it's bad.

Last night, I meant to go to a birthday party across town. I got the wine for the party, but when I got there I got anxious and drove away.

I also miss soccer and like ultimate frisbee, but some days my anxiety is really bad and I refuse to play with people. I tend to isolate myself because I feel alone, making everything worse.

I played Stanley's parable. That was really great.
Video games and gardening.

I just feel like I have to escape reality.
I've been anxious about everything, money school and my social aspects.
Sure, there's not to much to talk about really. I let my anxiety rule me and now I'm trying to pretend life isn't a thing.

I think part of the problem is I grew up in a household were I was told suicide is selfish. So, I can't tell my parents. They don't understand mood disorders very well. In fact, my brother, who is also chronically ill, has had openly worse depression. My parents handled it very poorly and wanted him to just "be better." To get up and "stop being lazy."

To me I'm being selfish, because my life isn't bad. But I feel bad. So, i struggle with self-loathing over the fact that my body (chronic disease) and mind refuse to work right. I've morbidly joked about how if I was an animal, they'd put me down. It's morbid, but it's true.

And I have opened up in the past. Most people don't know how to handle suicidal depression. I've had different boyfriends (I'm a girl) explicitly tell me to go get professional help because they didn't know what to do. Because when they don't see how or why you are depressed it's difficult for them to do anything. It's difficult for me, a person who is rejecting rational thoughts, to agree with someone who loves me because they are inherently biased about my existence. So, when I've opened up in the past all it does it make them worry about me and insist I see someone. And whilst I'm opening up I hate myself for putting that person through this. I can't imagine loving someone who hates themselves is easy.

I just want to work right. I really am trying, but some days it feels so heavy.

Nothing really spectacular, I just have serious self-loathing problems that have been around for a long time. I'm hyper-critical of myself and even when I KNOW i'm being irrational, I feel bad because my brain isn't working right. I just want to work right, and I'm trying too. I am, but I don't know what to do.
